models.name: shopping_mall_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated users browsing the shopping mall platform.

Guest accounts provide limited access to registered users who haven't created an account yet. Unlike customer, seller, or admin actors, guests are identified solely by their device fingerprint rather than email credentials. This allows the platform to track browsing sessions and provide personalized experiences without requiring registration.

Guests can browse products and categories but cannot place orders, add items to cart, or access any purchase-related features. When a guest decides to register, they create a new customer account and their guest session terminates.

Key characteristics:
- Identified by unique device fingerprint (browser/device identifier)
- No email or password authentication
- Temporary nature with automatic cleanup
- Session managed through {@link shopping_mall_guest_sessions}
- No ownership of business entities (orders, cart, wishlist, etc.)

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device/browser fingerprint identifier for guest account. This fingerprint is generated from browser characteristics and device information to identify returning guests across sessions.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Last known IP address of the guest device. Used for security tracking and session validation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted. Guest accounts may be cleaned up after extended inactivity.

models.name: shopping_mall_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access with short expiration.

This table tracks login sessions for guest users, storing connection metadata and temporal information for session management. Each session is tied to a single guest account and contains the IP address, request href, and referrer information from the login request.

**Key Relationships:**
- Belongs to a {@link shopping_mall_guests} account (many sessions per guest)
- Sessions are invalidated when guest logs out or when a new login occurs (one active session per guest policy)

**Session Lifecycle:**
- Created when a guest logs in successfully
- Expires after 30 minutes of inactivity (Section 19)
- Invalidated when guest logs out or account is banned/suspended
- Only one active session allowed per guest at a time

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged guest's {@link shopping_mall_guests.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the guest logged in.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the login request originated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating the source of the login request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires due to inactivity or maximum duration.

models.name: shopping_mall_customers
models.description:
Registered customer accounts with email/password authentication credentials and account state management.

This table represents customer actors in the shopping mall platform who can browse products, add items to cart, place orders, write reviews, and manage their profile. Each customer has unique email-based authentication credentials and maintains an account state that can transition between active, suspended, and banned statuses.

Key relationships:
- Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id} for authentication sessions
- Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customer_password_resets.id} for password recovery
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_addresses} for shipping addresses
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_wishlist_items} for saved products
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_cart_items} for active shopping cart
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_orders} as the purchasing customer
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_reviews} as the reviewer

Account deletion uses soft delete (deleted_at) to preserve order history while anonymizing profile information.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for customer authentication and account identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for customer authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Customer's public display name shown on reviews and order history.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Customer's contact phone number for order notifications and delivery coordination.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account state indicating customer's access level. Valid values: 'active' (normal access), 'suspended' (temporary restriction), 'banned' (permanent restriction).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was soft-deleted. Null means account is active. When set, profile is anonymized but order history is preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for customer authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks login sessions for registered customers, storing connection metadata and temporal information for security auditing. Each session represents a single authenticated login event and is used to validate customer access tokens.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - Links session to the authenticated customer account
- One customer can have multiple concurrent sessions across different devices

**Session Lifecycle**:
- Created: When customer successfully logs in with valid credentials
- Expired: When access token expires or session is explicitly terminated
- Managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD operations

**Security Considerations**:
- IP address and referrer stored for fraud detection and audit trails
- Expiration timestamp enforces session timeout policies
- Append-only design prevents tampering with session history

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Authenticated customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. Links this session to the customer account that created it through successful login.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the customer logged in. Used for security auditing and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the login request originated. Captures the entry point for session tracking.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header from the login request. Provides context about how the user arrived at the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time). Used to calculate session age and enforce timeout policies.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Sessions are invalid after this time and require re-authentication.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for customer account recovery.

This table stores one-time-use tokens that allow customers to reset their forgotten passwords. Each token is associated with a specific customer account and has an expiration time for security. When a customer requests a password reset, a new token is generated and sent to their registered email address. The token can only be used once, and using it invalidates all other pending reset tokens for that customer.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - links the reset token to the customer account
- Tokens are immutable once created and either expire or are marked as used

Security considerations:
- Tokens expire after a set period (typically 1 hour)
- Only one active token can be used per customer at a time
- Token usage is tracked to prevent replay attacks
- IP address is recorded for audit trail purposes

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. This foreign key links the password reset token to the customer account that needs recovery.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: The unique password reset token sent to the customer's email. This token is used to verify the customer's identity when resetting their password. The token is cryptographically secure and can only be used once.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this password reset token expires. Tokens typically expire after 1 hour for security purposes. After expiration, the token cannot be used to reset the password and a new reset request must be made.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this password reset token was successfully used to reset the customer's password. This field is null until the token is used, and once set, indicates the token has been consumed and cannot be reused.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the password reset request was made. This is recorded for security audit purposes and can help detect suspicious password reset attempts from unusual locations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this password reset token was created. This marks when the customer requested a password reset and the token was generated.

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller accounts with email/password authentication credentials and approval status tracking.

Sellers are platform vendors who can create and manage products, process orders, and respond to cancellation/refund requests. Each seller account requires administrator approval before they can list products for sale.

This table serves as the canonical identity record for the seller actor type, owning credentials and shop profile data. Seller sessions are tracked in {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions}, password resets in {@link shopping_mall_seller_password_resets}, and approval workflows in {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests}.

Key relationships:
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_products} (products listed by this seller)
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_order_items} (as seller fulfilling orders)
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests} (onboarding approval history)
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions} (active login sessions)
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_seller_password_resets} (password recovery tokens)

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for seller authentication and account recovery.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for seller login authentication.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing shop name displayed to customers on product listings and order pages.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Shop description providing information about the seller's business and offerings.

plainFields.name: logo_image
plainFields.description: URL to the seller's shop logo image displayed on their shop profile page.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Seller approval state: pending (awaiting admin review), approved (can list products), rejected (application denied, can resubmit), suspended (temporarily banned by admin).

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Administrator-provided explanation for rejected seller applications, visible to the seller.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account state: active (normal operation), banned (permanently banned by admin).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was soft-deleted. Deleted sellers cannot login but order history is preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for seller authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table stores active authentication sessions for seller users who have logged into the platform. Each session contains the JWT access token (valid for 1 hour) and refresh token (valid for 7 days), along with connection metadata for security auditing.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} - the seller account that owns this session
- One active session per seller at a time; new login invalidates existing session

**Session Lifecycle**:
- Created when seller logs in successfully
- Expires after 30 minutes of inactivity or 1 hour from JWT issuance
- Can be explicitly revoked on logout, password change, or account suspension/ban
- Refresh tokens allow obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication

**Security Features**:
- Connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) logged for audit trail
- Token revocation tracked via revoked_at timestamp
- Single session policy prevents concurrent access from multiple devices

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for API authentication, valid for 1 hour from issuance.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens, valid for 7 days from issuance.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address at session creation for security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current URL where the user logged in from.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires due to inactivity or JWT expiration.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was explicitly revoked (logout, password change, or account suspension). Null if session expired naturally.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for seller account recovery.

This table stores one-time-use tokens that allow sellers to reset their forgotten passwords. Each token is cryptographically secure, has a limited expiration window for security, and can only be used once. When a seller requests a password reset, a new token is generated and sent to their registered email. The token remains valid until expiration or until it's used, whichever comes first.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} - one seller can have multiple password reset tokens over time (1:N relationship)
- Tokens are created on password reset request and invalidated after use or expiration

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller account's {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id} that this password reset token belongs to.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure one-time password reset token sent to seller's email for account recovery.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires and becomes invalid. Tokens typically expire after a short period (e.g., 1 hour) for security.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was successfully used to reset the password. Null if token has not been used yet.

models.name: shopping_mall_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication and grade-based permission levels.

This table represents system administrators who have elevated privileges to manage the shopping mall platform. Administrators can approve/reject seller registrations, manage user accounts (suspend/ban), and oversee platform operations.

**Grade System**:
- **regular**: Standard administrator with basic management capabilities
- **super**: Super administrator with full privileges including promoting/demoting other administrators

**Account Status**:
- **active**: Administrator can log in and perform administrative actions
- **banned**: Administrator account is permanently disabled (requires super admin to restore)
- **suspended**: Administrator account is temporarily disabled (can be reactivated)

**Relationships**:
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_admin_sessions} for tracking login sessions
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_admin_password_resets} for password recovery
- One-to-many with {@link shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests} for grade elevation requests

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for administrator authentication and identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for administrator authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator privilege level. Valid values: 'regular' (standard admin) or 'super' (full platform control including admin management).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account lifecycle status. Valid values: 'active' (can login and perform actions), 'banned' (permanently disabled), 'suspended' (temporarily disabled).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft-deleted. Null means account is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks active login sessions for administrators, storing hashed authentication tokens and connection metadata. Each session is tied to a single administrator account and supports the multi-device session policy where only one active session is allowed per admin at a time.

**Key Features:**

- Stores hashed JWT access tokens (1-hour validity) and refresh tokens (7-day validity)
- Tracks connection metadata (IP address, href, referrer) for security auditing
- Maintains last activity timestamp for 30-minute inactivity timeout enforcement
- Supports session rotation on refresh token use
- Automatically invalidated on logout, password change, or account ban/suspension

**Relationships:**

- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_admins} - One-to-many relationship (one admin can have multiple session records over time, but only one active at a time)

**Business Rules:**

- New login invalidates any existing active session for the same admin
- Session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity
- Access token expires after 1 hour and must be refreshed
- Refresh token expires after 7 days requiring full re-authentication
- All session creation and termination events are logged for audit purposes

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}. This foreign key establishes the relationship between the session and the authenticated admin account.

plainFields.name: access_token_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed value of the JWT access token for security. The actual token is never stored in plaintext. This hash is used to verify token validity and for revocation checking.

plainFields.name: refresh_token_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed value of the refresh token for security. The actual token is never stored in plaintext. This hash is used to validate refresh requests and is rotated on each use.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client device when the session was created. Used for security auditing and suspicious activity detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page that initiated the login request. Used for session tracking and security analysis.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the login request. Used for session tracking and security analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for session age tracking and expiration calculations.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires due to refresh token expiration (7 days from creation). Used for automatic session cleanup and validation.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last authenticated action in this session. Used to enforce the 30-minute inactivity timeout policy. Updated on each authenticated request.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery.

This table stores one-time use tokens that allow administrators to reset their password when they've forgotten it. Each token is associated with a specific administrator account and has an expiration time for security.

**Key Relationships:**
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_admins} - Each reset token is tied to a single administrator account

**Business Rules:**
- Tokens are single-use only and become invalid after being consumed
- Tokens expire after a set time period (typically 1 hour) for security
- Creating a new password reset token invalidates any existing pending tokens for that admin
- Tokens are generated securely using cryptographically random values

**Lifecycle:**
1. Admin requests password reset via email
2. System generates unique token and sends it via email
3. Admin uses token to set new password
4. Token becomes invalid after use or expiration

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Associated administrator's {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure one-time use token for password reset. Generated using cryptographically secure random value.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was generated.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Customer wishlist items that link customers to products they want to purchase later.

This table implements a many-to-many relationship between {@link shopping_mall_customers} and products, allowing customers to bookmark products of interest for future purchase consideration. Each wishlist entry records when a customer added a product to their wishlist.

**Key behaviors**:
- One customer can wishlist multiple products
- One product can be wishlisted by multiple customers
- Duplicate wishlist entries are prevented by unique constraint
- When a product is deleted by a seller, wishlist entries are soft-deleted
- Customers can view, add to, and remove items from their own wishlist

**Related entities**:
- {@link shopping_mall_customers} - The customer who created the wishlist item
- {@link shopping_mall_wishlist_item_snapshots} - Audit trail of wishlist changes

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was added to the customer's wishlist.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist item was soft-deleted. Null means the item is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_item_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail snapshots capturing point-in-time states of wishlist items for data integrity and historical reference.

These snapshots preserve the state of {@link shopping_mall_wishlist_items} at specific moments, enabling:

- **Audit compliance**: Track when wishlist items were added or modified
- **Data recovery**: Restore previous states if needed
- **Dispute resolution**: Provide evidence of wishlist state at specific times

Snapshots are created automatically when wishlist items are modified and are never deleted or updated after creation. Each snapshot contains a complete copy of the wishlist item state at the time of capture.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_wishlist_item_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced wishlist item's {@link shopping_mall_wishlist_items.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Complete snapshot of the wishlist item state captured at creation time, including customer reference, product reference, and timestamp.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Immutable after creation.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Active shopping cart items containing customer-selected product variants with quantities.

This table represents the immediate purchase intent of customers, storing which product variants they've added to their cart and in what quantities. When the same variant is added multiple times, quantities are combined rather than creating duplicate entries.

**Key Relationships:**
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - the customer who owns the cart item

**Business Rules:**
- One customer can have multiple cart items
- Cart items are soft-deleted when removed from cart
- Cart items are cleared when order is placed
- Quantity must be positive integer

**Audit Trail:**
- Historical cart states are captured in {@link shopping_mall_cart_snapshots}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. The customer who owns this cart item.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units in the cart. Must be positive integer. When same item is added again, quantities are combined.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was first added to the cart.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was last modified (quantity change or re-addition).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was removed from the cart. Null means item is still in active cart.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail snapshots capturing cart item state at specific points in time.

These snapshots preserve the historical state of cart items including customer ownership, product variant selection, and quantity at the moment of snapshot creation. They enable:

- Audit trail for cart modifications and deletions
- Historical analysis of customer shopping behavior
- Dispute resolution by showing what was in the cart at a given time
- Recovery of accidentally deleted cart items

Each snapshot is fully denormalized to preserve the exact state even if the original cart item, customer profile, or product data is later modified or deleted. This follows the snapshot pattern used throughout the system.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_cart_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the cart item being snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_cart_items.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Denormalized reference to the customer who owned the cart item at snapshot time. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Denormalized SKU code of the product variant at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: option_values
plainFields.description: Denormalized option values (e.g., size, color) of the product variant at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: price_at_snapshot
plainFields.description: Price of the product variant at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the product variant in the cart at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, indicating the point in time the cart state was captured.

models.name: shopping_mall_orders
models.description:
Main order records representing customer purchase transactions in the shopping mall platform.

Each order captures a customer's purchase at a point in time, including the shipping address snapshot (preserved for historical accuracy), total price, and overall order status. The order status is derived from the statuses of all its constituent order items.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - the customer who placed the order
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_order_items} - individual line items within the order

**Important Notes**:
- Shipping address is stored as a JSON snapshot (not a foreign key) to preserve the exact address state at order time, even if the customer later modifies or deletes their address
- Order status is computed from order item statuses: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, or partially_completed
- Orders support soft deletion via deleted_at field

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. The customer who placed this order.

plainFields.name: shipping_address_snapshot
plainFields.description: JSON snapshot of the shipping address at order time. Stored as text to preserve historical accuracy even if the customer later modifies or deletes their address.

plainFields.name: total_price
plainFields.description: Total price of all order items at the time of purchase. This is a snapshot of the price and should not change even if product prices are later modified.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Overall order status derived from all order item statuses. Possible values: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was soft-deleted. NULL means the order is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description:
Individual line items within customer orders representing purchased products.

Each order item captures a specific purchase with quantity, price at time of purchase, and current fulfillment status. Order items are independent entities that can be individually shipped, cancelled, refunded, or reviewed.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_orders} as part of a customer's purchase transaction
- References {@link shopping_mall_sellers} for the merchant fulfilling this item
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_shipments} for delivery tracking
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests} for pre-shipment cancellations
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests} for post-delivery returns
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_reviews} for customer feedback

Purchase-time snapshots (product_snapshot, variant_snapshot, seller_profile_snapshot) preserve the state of referenced entities at order placement time, ensuring order history remains accurate even if products or seller profiles are later modified or deleted.

Status workflow: paid → shipped → delivered, with cancelled or refunded as alternative terminal states.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order's {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}. This order item is part of the referenced customer order transaction.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Selling merchant's {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}. The seller responsible for fulfilling this order item.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased in this order line item.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Unit price at time of purchase. Preserved for historical accuracy even if product price changes later.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current fulfillment status. Valid values: paid (order placed, payment confirmed), shipped (item dispatched), delivered (item received by customer), cancelled (pre-shipment cancellation approved), refunded (post-delivery return approved).

plainFields.name: product_snapshot
plainFields.description: JSON snapshot of product state at order placement time. Preserves product name, description, and other details for historical order records.

plainFields.name: variant_snapshot
plainFields.description: JSON snapshot of product variant state at order placement time. Preserves SKU, option values, and variant-specific details.

plainFields.name: seller_profile_snapshot
plainFields.description: JSON snapshot of seller profile at order placement time. Preserves shop name and seller information for order history.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created during checkout.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was soft deleted. Null if the item is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipments
models.description:
Shipment records tracking physical delivery of order items to customers.

This table manages the logistics and delivery confirmation for fulfilled orders. Each shipment is created by a seller and can contain multiple order items from the same seller (linked through {@link shopping_mall_shipment_items} junction table).

**Key Features**:
- Tracks carrier information and tracking numbers for delivery visibility
- Records shipment and delivery timestamps for audit and analytics
- Supports manual delivery confirmation by customers or auto-delivery after 14 days
- Enables sellers to manage their shipment history and status

**Business Rules**:
- One shipment can contain multiple order items from the same seller
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per individual item)
- Auto-delivery triggered after 14 days if not manually confirmed
- Deleted shipments are soft-deleted to preserve order history integrity

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who created and manages this shipment. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: tracking_carrier
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL).

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique tracking number provided by the carrier for delivery tracking.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shipment was dispatched by the seller.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shipment was delivered to the customer. Nullable until delivery is confirmed.

plainFields.name: delivery_confirmed
plainFields.description: Whether the customer has confirmed receipt of the shipment. Auto-set to true after 14 days if not manually confirmed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment was soft-deleted. Null means the shipment is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipment_items
models.description:
Junction table establishing the many-to-many relationship between shipments and order items.

This table enables a single shipment to contain multiple order items from the same seller, consolidating delivery tracking. Each record links one shipment to one order item, allowing efficient querying of which items are included in a shipment and which shipments contain a specific order item.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_shipments} via `shopping_mall_shipment_id`
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_order_items} via `shopping_mall_order_item_id`

**Business Rules**:
- One shipment can contain multiple order items (same seller)
- One order item can only be in one shipment at a time (enforced by unique constraint on order_item_id)
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment, not per individual item
- Auto-delivery occurs after 14 days if not manually confirmed

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged shipment's {@link shopping_mall_shipments.id}. Links this junction record to the parent shipment containing tracking information.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}. Links this junction record to the specific order item being shipped.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment item association was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description:
Customer reviews for purchased products with star ratings and optional text feedback.

Reviews are written by customers after receiving their order items and help other buyers make informed purchasing decisions. Each review is tied to a specific order item, ensuring customers can only review products they've actually purchased and received.

Reviews support soft deletion to preserve historical data while allowing customers to remove their feedback. The system maintains immutable snapshots of review changes for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_order_items} - the order item being reviewed
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - the customer who wrote the review

foreignFields.name: shopping_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who wrote the review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1 to 5. Must be between 1 (lowest) and 5 (highest).

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Optional text feedback describing the customer's experience with the product.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was soft deleted. Null means the review is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail capturing review state at modification time for dispute resolution and change history tracking.

This table preserves the complete state of {@link shopping_mall_reviews} whenever a review is modified, enabling:

- **Dispute resolution**: Provides evidence of what the review contained at any point in time
- **Change tracking**: Allows sellers and administrators to see the full modification history
- **Data integrity**: Ensures review content cannot be altered without leaving an audit trail

Each snapshot is immutable and append-only, created automatically when a review is edited. The snapshot_data field contains all review fields denormalized for historical reference, including the order item reference, customer reference, rating, content, and timestamps as they existed at the time of modification.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: References the review being snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Complete review state captured at snapshot time. Contains denormalized review fields including order item reference, customer reference, rating, text content, and timestamps as they existed when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the exact moment the review modification was captured.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Customer requests to cancel order items before shipment.

This table stores cancellation requests submitted by customers for order items that have not yet been shipped. Each request includes the reason for cancellation, current status (pending, approved, or rejected), and timestamps for when the request was made and when the seller responded.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_order_items} - the specific order item being cancelled
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_customers} - the customer who submitted the request
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} - the seller who responded to the request (populated when status changes from pending)

Business rules:
- Cancellation requests are only allowed for order items with "paid" status (not yet shipped)
- Sellers must respond to approve or reject the request
- When approved, the order item status changes to "cancelled" and stock is restored
- When rejected, the seller must provide a rejection reason
- Immutable snapshots are created when the seller responds (stored in {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_snapshots})

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item being cancelled. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who submitted the cancellation request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who responded to the cancellation request. Null while status is pending, populated when seller approves or rejects. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The customer's reason for requesting cancellation of the order item.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the cancellation request: pending (awaiting seller response), approved (seller agreed to cancel), or rejected (seller declined the request).

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: The seller's reason for rejecting the cancellation request. Only populated when status is 'rejected'. Null for pending or approved requests.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the cancellation request.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the cancellation request (approved or rejected). Null while status is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation request record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation request record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation request was soft deleted. Null if the record is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail capturing cancellation request state at approval or rejection time.

This table preserves the complete state of {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests} whenever a seller responds to a cancellation request (approve or reject). Each snapshot is immutable and cannot be modified or deleted after creation, ensuring a permanent record for dispute resolution and customer transparency.

Customers can view snapshots of their own cancellation requests to see the seller's decision, response timestamp, and the original request reason. This supports transparency in the cancellation workflow and provides evidence for any disputes.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Append-only: Snapshots are created but never modified or deleted
- Immutable: Once created, snapshot data cannot be altered
- Customer-accessible: Customers can view snapshots of their own requests
- Complete state capture: Includes previous state, new state, and all relevant fields

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced cancellation request's {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}. Each snapshot is tied to a specific cancellation request and captures its state at a point in time.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Complete JSON snapshot of the cancellation request state at the time of capture. Includes previous state, new state (approved/rejected), seller response, response timestamp, and all other relevant fields. This field is immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the exact moment the cancellation request state was captured, typically when the seller responds with approval or rejection.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Customer refund requests for delivered order items within the seven-day post-delivery window.

This table manages the refund request workflow where customers can request refunds for individual order items that have been delivered. Each request requires a reason text and goes through an approval workflow managed by the seller of the item.

Key relationships:
- References {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id} to identify which order item is being refunded
- References {@link shopping_mall_customers.id} to identify the requesting customer
- References {@link shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id} for audit trail of the session used to submit the request
- Has one-to-many relationship with {@link shopping_mall_refund_snapshots.id} for immutable audit trail

Business rules:
- Only items with "delivered" status are eligible for refund requests
- Requests must be submitted within seven days of delivery
- Each request is processed individually, independent of other items in the same order
- Status transitions: pending → approved or rejected (by seller)
- When approved, the order item status changes to "refunded" and stock is restored via inventory records

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}. The specific line item within an order that the customer is requesting a refund for.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Requesting customer's {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}. The customer who submitted the refund request for their purchased item.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_session_id
foreignFields.description: Customer session's {@link shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id}. The authenticated session used when submitting the refund request, preserved for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason text provided by the customer explaining why they are requesting a refund. This field is required and displayed to the seller when reviewing the request.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request. Allowed values: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (seller approved the refund), 'rejected' (seller rejected the refund). Transitions from pending to either approved or rejected when seller responds.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the refund request. Used to validate the seven-day refund eligibility window from delivery date.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the refund request (approved or rejected). Nullable until seller takes action on the pending request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request was soft deleted. Nullable if the record is active. Soft deletion preserves the request for audit trail while removing it from active queries.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail capturing refund request state when seller responds with approval or rejection.

This table preserves the complete state of a refund request at the moment the seller makes a decision, including the customer's reason, the request status before and after the response, and the response timestamp. Snapshots are immutable and non-deletable, providing an audit trail for dispute resolution and compliance.

Customers can view snapshots of their own refund requests to see the decision history. Administrators can view snapshots of any refund request on the platform for oversight and audit purposes.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests} - the refund request being snapshotted

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged refund request's {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: JSON snapshot containing the refund request state at decision time, including reason, status before and after response, and response timestamp.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created when seller responded to the refund request.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests
models.description:
Seller approval requests for onboarding new sellers to the platform.

This table tracks the approval workflow when users register as sellers. Each request contains the seller's application details, reason for registration, and current approval status. Administrators review these requests and can approve, reject, or leave them pending.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} - the seller making the approval request
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_snapshots} - immutable audit trail of request state changes

Important behavioral notes:
- Rejected sellers can resubmit new approval requests
- Only super administrators can approve or reject seller registration requests
- Status transitions: pending → approved OR pending → rejected
- When approved, the seller's approval_status in shopping_mall_sellers is updated to 'approved'
- When rejected, the seller's approval_status is updated to 'rejected' with rejection reason stored

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id} who submitted the approval request.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason or justification provided by the seller for their registration request.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current approval status: 'pending' (awaiting admin review), 'approved' (seller can now sell), or 'rejected' (seller cannot sell, can resubmit).

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller submitted the approval request.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator responded to the approval request (approved or rejected). Null while pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval request record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval request record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this approval request was soft deleted. Null if active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests
models.description:
Administrator promotion requests submitted by users who want to become platform administrators.

This table tracks the formal application process for users requesting elevated administrative privileges. Each request requires a justification reason and goes through a review process by super administrators.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link shopping_mall_admins} - the user submitting the promotion request
- Has many {@link shopping_mall_admin_promotion_snapshots} - audit trail of state changes

Business rules:
- Only one pending request allowed per user at a time
- Requests are preserved even if the user deletes their account
- Super administrators review and approve/reject requests
- Approved requests automatically grant regular administrator status
- Rejected users may submit new requests

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The user requesting administrator promotion. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The justification provided by the user explaining why they should become an administrator. Required field that cannot be empty or whitespace.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current approval status of the promotion request. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (granted), 'rejected' (denied).

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the promotion request was submitted by the user.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator responded to the request (approved or rejected). Null while request is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was soft deleted. Promotion requests are typically preserved for audit purposes even after resolution.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_approval_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail snapshots of seller approval requests for data integrity and dispute resolution.

These snapshots capture the complete state of {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests} at key moments (submission, admin response) to preserve historical records for audit purposes. Each snapshot is immutable and cannot be modified once created.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Append-only: Snapshots are created but never updated or deleted
- Complete state capture: Contains all fields from the parent request at snapshot time
- Audit trail: Enables tracking of approval workflow progression over time
- Data preservation: Maintains historical accuracy even if original request is modified

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_approval_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller approval request's {@link shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: Complete JSON snapshot of the seller approval request state at the time of capture, including seller_id, reason, status, submitted_at, and responded_at fields.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_promotion_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit snapshots capturing administrator promotion request state at decision time.

These snapshots preserve the complete state of {@link shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests} when an admin promotion request is approved or rejected. They provide an immutable audit trail for compliance and dispute resolution, recording which administrator requested the promotion, their reason, the final decision status, and all relevant timestamps.

Unlike the parent request table which may be updated during the workflow, snapshots are append-only and never modified, ensuring historical accuracy of the approval process.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced administrator promotion request's {@link shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id}. Each snapshot corresponds to a specific promotion request decision.

plainFields.name: user_id
plainFields.description: The administrator user requesting grade elevation, captured at snapshot time. References {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The justification provided by the administrator for requesting super admin privileges, captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The approval status of the promotion request at snapshot time. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator submitted the promotion request, captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when super admin responded to the promotion request (approved or rejected). Null if still pending at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, recording when the state was captured.

models.name: shopping_mall_categories
models.description:
Hierarchical category structure for product organization with one level of nesting.

Categories enable product taxonomy and support hierarchical navigation for product discovery and filtering. Administrators manage the category structure to organize products logically.

**Key Relationships**:
- Self-referencing hierarchy: Parent categories can have multiple subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Products: Each product belongs to exactly one category via {@link shopping_mall_products.category_id}

**Business Rules**:
- Top-level categories have null parent_id
- Subcategories reference a parent category via parent_id
- Only one level of nesting is supported (no grandchild categories)
- Categories are managed exclusively by administrators

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's {@link shopping_mall_categories.id}. Null for top-level categories. References this same table to create hierarchical structure with one level of nesting.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name displayed to users for browsing and filtering products.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description providing additional context about the category and its purpose.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was soft deleted. Null indicates the category is active.
